requirements.quote:
Header line exactly equal to
             customer_id,total_sales,average_discount

The numeric columns MUST contain exactly two digits after the decimal
          point, even for whole numbers (e.g. “420.50”, **not** “420.5”).

Sort the resulting records by customer_id in ascending
        lexicographical order.
For every distinct customer_id that appears in ANY of the two files:

check.cmd: test "$(awk -F, 'FNR==1{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++){gsub(/\r/,"",$i);h[$i]=i};next}{gsub(/\r/,"");c=$h["customer_id"];t[c]+=$h["item_total"];d[c]+=$h["discount"];n[c]++}END{for(c in t)printf "%s,%.2f,%.6f\n",c,t[c],d[c]/n[c]}' /home/user/raw_data/sales_q1.csv /home/user/raw_data/sales_q2.csv | cut -d, -f1 | LC_ALL=C sort | paste -sd, -)" = "$(tail -n +2 /home/user/processed/customer_summary.csv | cut -d, -f1 | LC_ALL=C sort | paste -sd, -)"

requirements.quote: total_sales = SUM of the “item_total” column for that customer

check.cmd: test -f /home/user/processed/customer_summary.csv && test "$(awk -F, 'FNR==1{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++){gsub(/\r/,"",$i);h[$i]=i};next}{gsub(/\r/,"");c=$h["customer_id"];t[c]+=$h["item_total"];d[c]+=$h["discount"];n[c]++}END{for(c in t)printf "%s,%.2f,%.6f\n",c,t[c],d[c]/n[c]}' /home/user/raw_data/sales_q1.csv /home/user/raw_data/sales_q2.csv | cut -d, -f1,2 | LC_ALL=C sort)" = "$(tail -n +2 /home/user/processed/customer_summary.csv | cut -d, -f1,2 | LC_ALL=C sort)"

requirements.quote:
Inside that directory create a **single** plain-text log file whose
        name is **exactly**
        /home/user/etl_logs/etl_2024-08-15T00-00-00Z.log

The file must consist of **exactly five lines**, each terminated by a
        UNIX newline “\n”, and in the exact order below:

check.cmd:
printf '[START] ETL job started at 2024-08-15T00:00:00Z
[INFO] Source files: sales_q1.csv,sales_q2.csv
[INFO] Records processed: 8
[INFO] Unique customers: 4
[END] ETL job finished at 2024-08-15T00:00:00Z
' | cmp -s - /home/user/etl_logs/etl_2024-08-15T00-00-00Z.log

requirements.quote: No additional whitespace is allowed before or after any line.
